question: What are the two hourly volume thresholds in All-Way Stop Control Warrant D, and how can they be adjusted when the major-street 85th-percentile speed exceeds 40 mph?
model_answer: Direct Answer: All-Way Stop Control Warrant D (8-Hour Volume) uses two thresholds: the combined motor vehicle, bicycle, and pedestrian volume entering from the major-street approaches must be at least 300 units per hour, and the combined volume entering from the minor-street approaches must be at least 200 units per hour, for each of any 8 hours of a typical day (the same 8 hours for both). When the 85th-percentile approach speed on the major street exceeds 40 mph, these minimum vehicular volume values may be reduced to 70 percent (i.e., approximately 210 and 140 units per hour, respectively). Options (permitted): - All-way stop control may be installed where an engineering study indicates: "The combined motor vehicle, bicycle, and pedestrian volume entering the intersection from the major-street approaches is at least 300 units per hour for each of any 8 hours of a typical day," and "The combined motor vehicle, bicycle, and pedestrian volume entering the intersection from the minor-street approaches is at least 200 units per hour for each of any of the same 8 hours." - "If the 85th-percentile approach speed of the major-street traffic exceeds 40 mph, the minimum vehicular volume warrants may be reduced to 70 percent of the values given in Items A and B in Paragraph 1 of this Section." Visual evidence: - [Image 5] shows Section 2B.16, All-Way Stop Control Warrant D, including the 300 units per hour major-street and 200 units per hour minor-street thresholds in Paragraph 1 and the 70 percent reduction option in Paragraph 2. Citations: - Section 2B.16 Option §2 (p.79) - Page 120
gold_answer: For the same 8 hours of a typical day, the combined entering volume must be at least 300 units per hour on the major-street approaches and at least 200 units per hour on the minor-street approaches. If the major-street 85th-percentile speed exceeds 40 mph, the minimums may be reduced to 70 percent of those values.
